body: A hammer and unopened nails sit beside a note. It says to brace the garden-side door before the next treatment. It doesn't say who will return.
title: Hammer and nails

body:
Notebook page: “fortify here” meant boards over the garden door before the next patrol came through. A man with a clipboard took our names and told us to say nothing about the count.

My mother put it with the household bills so it would not be thrown away. It was the only part of the week that still had a date.
title: Diary page

body:
Diary margin: the first heart marks the cot where the orchard crew slept after the spray run. Their boots left a sweet yellow dust; the family returned before anyone posted a warning.

I wrote it down at the time, before the dust was swept. The cot's blanket still smelled sweet a week later.
title: Notepad page

body:
On the photograph back: second heart, our spare blanket. I rinsed green flecks from it after the seed-treatment men left, then the well began tasting of pennies.

I kept the corner of the old page in my pocket. The flecks came out of the blanket slowly, and the well water was cloudy for days.
title: Receipt

body:
Torn notebook page: the third heart is the room lent to two pasture-test workers. One wrote that the calves refused water after the pasture was sprayed.

Their boots by the door were caked with the same pale dust as the pasture gate. I wrote this down before their truck left.
title: Photograph

body:
Personal note: at the fourth heart we shut the window during the field misting. The kitchen herbs curled by supper, hours before the road patrol appeared.

I set it aside to show the neighbor when she returned. Her porch was empty by the time the light was good enough to read it.

There may be a simple reason for the change. Nobody at the next stop could tell us what to do with the first version.
title: Notebook page

body:
Letter draft: the fifth heart was for the baby room. A soldier at the roadblock told us to keep the children indoors, but would not put the order in writing.

There was a numbered tag on our door the next morning. I wrote the date here while I could still remember it.
title: Handwritten letter
